name: Chin-Up
description: The chin-up is a vertical pulling bodyweight exercise performed with a supinated (underhand) grip. The supinated grip places the biceps in a mechanically advantageous position, increasing their contribution compared to the pull-up. The chin-up is often considered slightly easier for beginners and provides excellent simultaneous stimulation of the lats and biceps.

execution.starting_position: Hang from a bar with a supinated (palms facing you) grip at shoulder width or slightly narrower. Arms fully extended, core lightly engaged.
execution.setup_instructions: Grip the bar underhand at shoulder width. The narrower grip and supinated wrist position is what distinguishes this from a pull-up.
steps: Initiate the movement by depressing the shoulder blades.
Pull yourself up by driving the elbows down and toward your sides.
Continue until your chin is above the bar.
Lower under control until arms are fully extended.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the pull, inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Not reaching full extension at the bottom
safety_considerations: Avoid if experiencing acute biceps tendon pain
Fully extend at the bottom of each rep
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full dead hang at bottom, chin above bar at top.
coaching_cues: Pull the bar toward your chest rather than your chin toward the bar
Maintain proud posture — do not let the shoulders creep toward the ears
